title: Sales Blueprint versus solution architecture
objective: Classify 'prioritized use case list', 'implementation reference architecture' and 'executive value readout'.
clearance: Rewritten draft; pending SME and partner clearance

blocks.x: "Blueprint" means two different things at Glean. Keep them separate so customers know which conversation they are in.

items: **The Sales Blueprint (Blueprint Consultation)** is a pre-sales process. It covers discovery, workflow prioritization, business value, and the evaluation decision. Its outputs include a prioritized use case list, current-state and future-state workflow maps, an evidence-labeled value case, and an executive validation decision.

**The Customer Blueprint Framework** is a post-sales program led by Glean Solutions Architecture. Each blueprint is a reusable package for a recurring post-sales challenge: a problem statement, reference architecture and integration patterns, a recommended implementation path and governance model, and example assets. Examples include patterns for building many custom connectors and for optimizing infrastructure cost.

blocks.x: Architecture patterns can inform feasibility and delivery. If DITL shows that a use case depends on several custom connectors, a post-sales pattern may shape the effort estimate and the handoff plan. But an architecture pattern does not replace customer discovery or executive alignment. A connector pattern explains how something can be built. The Sales Blueprint explains why it matters to a specific team, how their work changes, and how success will be measured.

blocks.label: Boundary
blocks.x: Do not present architecture diagrams as proof of value. This accreditation does not replace technical architecture or connector accreditation.
The two artifacts share a word but answer different questions. Keep them separate in your notes and your scope.

blocks.title: Two kinds of blueprint
blocks.alt: A comparison of the Sales Blueprint, which decides whether and where to invest, with the Customer Blueprint Framework, which designs how the solution will be built and run.
